summaries.demographer: Pedro Jimenez is a 75-year-old married Mexican American man living with his wife Rosa in an owned home in Puyallup, Washington (Q05, Q51, Q58, Q84). He was born in Yakima, Washington, to parents from Jalisco, Mexico, grew up bilingual, completed tenth grade, and did not receive a high school diploma or GED (Q86, Q87, Q90). His household consists of two older adults on Social Security and Medicare, with three adult children and six grandchildren nearby or regionally connected (Q05, Q40, Q74). His life-course profile reflects early labor force entry, informal skilled manual work, homeownership, retirement, and continuing community participation through volunteering (Q01, Q16, Q65, Q67).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Pedro is strongly loss-averse and budget-conscious, using notebooks, receipts, savings buckets, and delayed purchases to manage uncertainty on a fixed income (Q17, Q56, Q61, Q64). He shows practical time preferences: he values immediate household stability, medical adherence, and home maintenance while still allowing modest splurges on tools, ingredients, or short trips when the budget permits (Q60, Q62, Q83). His decisions are motivated by self-sufficiency, family obligation, and avoiding dependence on children unless truly necessary (Q40, Q63, Q82). Peer influence works through trusted small networks, such as walking club accountability, doctor advice, Rosa's reminders, and family input rather than mass media or online persuasion (Q32, Q42, Q48).
summaries.political_scientist: Pedro is a vote-by-mail participant who votes in presidential and most local elections and pays particular attention to local measures, taxes, roads, schools, health care, and senior programs (Q23, Q24). He identifies as an Independent closer to the Democratic Party, with moderate, practical views shaped by Social Security, Medicare, immigration, working families, and skepticism toward partisan shouting (Q24, Q95, Q96). He expresses qualified trust in institutions: he trusts doctors and official health sources but is cautious about policing and recognizes unequal treatment by race and ethnicity (Q20, Q26, Q42). His civic participation is community-oriented rather than activist, expressed through voting, church support, neighbor help, and senior center volunteering (Q16, Q29, Q47).
summaries.psychologist: Pedro presents as conscientious, practical, modest, and relationally anchored, with identity built around usefulness, family responsibility, craftsmanship, faith, and cultural continuity (Q05, Q65, Q108, Q109). He regulates emotion through routine, gardening, prayer, walking, repair work, and family connection, while acknowledging worry, grief, and some anxiety without pursuing therapy (Q43, Q44, Q45, Q50). His cognitive style is methodical and concrete: he tracks budgets manually, checks blood pressure, plans around expenses, and trusts firsthand evidence and known authorities (Q17, Q31, Q42, Q56). He also has a quiet competitive streak and pride in competence, visible in repair demonstrations and careful workmanship, but his social style remains restrained and cooperative (Q16, Q65, Q77).
